voices.label: TOM 1
voices.name: Tom 1 (with run generator)
controls: Run generator: Run Threshold, Step Time, Run Time, Balance (sequential to random), Up/Down, On/Off, footswitch
voices.notes: Control list and order from the 1994 sample-disk README; 1985 reviews give the same set (Sensitivity, Filter Pitch, Filter Sweep, Tone Pitch, Bend, Decay, Noise/Tone, Click Level, Level, Second Skin). Exact printed legends not verified. Only Tom 1 has the run generator, which steps this drum's pitch sequentially or randomly on successive hits. Year 1985 is inferred from the Sept 1985 reviews.

voices.label: TOM 2
voices.name: Tom 2
voices.notes: Same voice circuit as Tom 1, no run generator.

voices.label: TOM 3
voices.name: Tom 3
voices.notes: Same voice circuit as Tom 1, no run generator.

voices.label: TOM 4
voices.name: Tom 4
voices.notes: Same voice circuit as Tom 1, no run generator.

accent: No accent control. Each tom is a pad-triggered analog voice with its own trigger-sensitivity control and LED; how hit strength changes level or tone is not described in the SDS 400 sources.
global_features: Four identical analog tom channels; same voice circuitry as the SDS 800 (tone oscillator, white noise, filter with sweep, click)
Second Skin: fixed-frequency modulation; subtle = double-headed tom, pushed = metallic clangs and ring-mod effects
Run generator on Tom 1 only: Run Threshold, Step Time, Run Time, Balance, Up/Down, On/Off; footswitch supplied; rear jack for remote on/off
Outputs: individual jack per tom, mono Mix (master volume), Stereo; headphone socket on the front
5-pin DIN socket for the SDS6 sequencer, Simmons CBM64 sequencer package or MPC programmers
No patch memory mentioned in any source (inferred: all settings are knobs)
Price GBP 549.99 inc VAT (Sept 1985)
pack_contents: 20 stereo 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs in one flat folder: Slap-1, Slap-2, Slap-3 (white-noise 'slap' sounds) and Tom-01 to Tom-17 (electronic toms; the README says some may pass as snares). Count, order and names match Hallvard Tangeraas's 1994 TX16W sample disk (SLAP_1.W01 to TOM_17.W20), so the folder is very likely a WAV conversion of it (inferred). Files are not tied to a particular tom channel. Mixed numbering (Slap-1 vs Tom-01). No gaps, no loops. Lengths 0.23 to 1.16 s.

maker: Simmons Electronic Drums (Dave Simmons, with Richard James Burgess); first units built by Musicaid

voices.label: BASS DRUM
voices.name: Bass drum module
controls: 4 memory buttons: 1 fixed factory preset + 3 user sounds
voices.notes: Standard module. One monophonic analog voice (triangle oscillator + noise). Played from the 22-inch hexagonal bass pad. Reviews list modules as bass, snare, three toms; the physical left-to-right rack order and printed legends are not verified.

voices.label: SNARE
voices.name: Snare drum module
controls: 4 memory buttons: 1 fixed factory preset + 3 user sounds
voices.notes: Standard module. There is no separate rim channel: the pad's metal rim gives rimshot-style tones through the same module (1981 review). The packs' Rimshot / Crack files are therefore snare-channel sounds (inferred).

voices.label: SNARE (rim)
voices.name: Snare module struck on the pad rim
voices.notes: Not a separate module; listed so rimshot samples can share the snare's choke group (inferred).

voices.label: TOM 1
voices.name: Tom tom module 1
controls: 4 memory buttons: 1 fixed factory preset + 3 user sounds
voices.notes: Standard module (three toms in the basic kit). Bend sweeps the pitch down (the classic Simmons tom).

voices.label: TOM 2
voices.name: Tom tom module 2
controls: 4 memory buttons: 1 fixed factory preset + 3 user sounds
voices.notes: Standard module.

voices.label: TOM 3
voices.name: Tom tom module 3
controls: 4 memory buttons: 1 fixed factory preset + 3 user sounds
voices.notes: Standard module. The rack takes up to 7 modules, so a 4th tom (as in the SDSV pack's 'tom 4') was possible (inferred).

voices.label: HI-HAT (closed)
voices.name: Hi-hat module (optional), pedal closed
controls: Hi-hat pedal input on the rack rear (open/closed)
voices.notes: Optional module; Music UK (1983) says the cymbal-type modules used digitally sampled sound passed through analog filters. One channel: the pedal moves it between closed and open.

voices.label: HI-HAT (open)
voices.name: Hi-hat module, pedal open
voices.notes: Not a separate module; listed so the packs' open-hat samples can share the hi-hat choke group.

voices.label: HI-HAT (pedal)
voices.name: Hi-hat module, pedal sound
voices.notes: Whether the hardware made a 'chick' sound from the pedal alone is unknown; the SDS-5 pack has two Hat Pedal files.

voices.label: CYMBAL
voices.name: Cymbal module (optional)
voices.notes: Optional sampled-cymbal module. None of the three packs contains a crash/ride sample.

accent: No accent switch. Dynamics come from how hard the pad is struck: the pads are pressure-sensitive (dynamic range shrinks as Sensitivity is raised), and hit strength also changes the attack through the Click/Drum control. Each channel also has a trigger input for a sequencer such as the SDS6.
global_features: Rack holds up to 7 sound modules plus an output mixer; basic kit = bass, snare and three tom modules
Each module stores 4 sounds, picked with a square of 4 push-buttons: top-left = fixed factory preset; 3 user sounds (two set on rows of screwdriver trim-pots, one on front-panel knobs)
Every channel is one monophonic analog voice; samples taken from the same module are alternative settings of one channel, not sounds that can play together
Optional hi-hat module (rear hi-hat pedal input) and cymbal module
Mixer: Sensitivity and Output level per channel
Outputs (all XLR): individual per channel, pre-panned stereo pair, mono mix
Per-channel external trigger inputs (SDS6 sequencer, TR-808, MC-4 etc.)
No built-in sequencer (SDS6 sold separately)
Pads: hexagonal, piezo pickup, polycarbonate surface; 22-inch bass pad

default_kit.sound: BASS DRUM (factory preset on the top-left memory button)

pack_contents: Three folders from the same machine; none labels which memory/preset a file came from. 'Simmons SDS-5': 64 stereo 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs in BASSDRUM (Bassdrum-01..12), SNARES (Snaredrum-01..21, Rimshot-01..07), Toms (Tom-01..17), CYMBALS (Hat Closed-01..03, Hat Open-01..02, Hat Pedal-01..02); numbered, no gaps, no crash/ride despite the CYMBALS name. 'Simmons SDS5': 23 mono WAVs with short names: SDKick01-04, SDSnare01-07, SDPop01-02, SDTomLo/Med/Mid/Hard/Noise/EHi/ELo, SDSTomE2 (naming outlier), SDHat_C, SDHat_O. 'Simmons SDSV': 45 mono WAVs: sds5_kits (SDS5 kick 1-3, Kick 4, Snare hi 1, snare hi 2, snare lo, snare mid, Crack, tom 1-4) and sds5_misc (SDS5 01-32, numbered only, no voice names). Four sds5_kits files are exactly 0.186 s long (possible truncation). No loops anywhere.

accent: ACCENT button adds accents on chosen steps, separately for each voice; the accent boost is preset internally per voice and cannot be adjusted. Pads are not velocity-sensitive. Polynominal says accent can also come from the pedal input; the HKA Design MIDI retrofit maps note velocity to accent.
global_features: Global PITCH slider moves all voices together (no per-voice tuning; not stored in memory)
SHIFT 0-3: randomly pushes/pulls beats for a human feel; level 3 gives a jazz-type swing
ACCURACY (quantise): 7 settings from 1/4-note triplets to 1/32-note triplets
Tempo 40-250 BPM with digital readout
100 patterns (00-99) of up to 99 beats; 100 songs; Copy, double length, Insert/Delete in songs
14 sliders: 11 voice levels (hats share one) + tempo, pitch, click volume
Outputs: 1/4-inch individual out per voice, pre-panned stereo L/R (mono from one jack)
Sync: To Tape click track at 24 pulses per quarter note; From Tape external drive; tape dump/verify
15-pin Trigger Inputs (5 V TTL) and External Voice connector
Hardware: Z80 CPU, 8-bit linear DAC (DAC0800), 52K PROM sample memory; 12-voice polyphony
No MIDI (later HKA Design retrofit)
pack_contents: 12 mono 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs in a subfolder 'mxr185', one per hardware voice, named 'MXR <sound>': Claps, Cowbell, Crash, Hat_closed, Hat_open, Kick, Rimshot, Snare, Tom 1, Tom 2, Tom 3, woodblock. global_features: 22 sampled sounds (8-bit PCM on EPROM) on 22 non-velocity pads; sequencer.de describes 'three sound groups (2x8 and 1x6)' matching the pad layout
8 voices: 8 voice level sliders (one per voice group) + master volume; sounds in a group share a slider and an individual output (e.g. common bass out, common snare out)
Outputs: stereo (sounds spread across the field), mono, 8 grouped individual outs, headphones, separate metronome out
48 patterns of up to 32 steps + 3 songs, kept on a battery-backed RAM cartridge; patterns cannot be programmed without the cartridge
Real-time recording in layers or step entry; tempo set with two wheels; 2-digit display
Roland DIN sync in/out; trigger inputs for drum pads
Alternative ROM sound sets (mid-1984) for the DPM-48E: Electronic Drums, Rock, Latin Percussion
No MIDI (FPB Synth retrofit uses the cartridge slot)
UK price GBP 699
pack_contents: 20 stereo 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs, flat folder: Agogo1, Agogo2, Bassdrum-01..03, Cabasa-01..02, Clap, Crash, Hat Closed-01..02, Hat Open, Ride, Rim, Snaredrum-01..02, Tom-01..04. These are the same 20 sounds as Kyle Farrell's sampling of the machine as converted by Hallvard Tangeraas (accenthh, agogo1-2, bass1-3, cabasa1-2, clap, closedhh, crash, openhh, ride, rim, snare1-2, tom1-4), so one of the two 'Hat Closed' files is probably the accent hi-hat (inferred). The 2 accent-only duplicates of the original 22 are missing. Not the KB6 set (which has 23 samples). Mixed naming (Agogo1 vs -01). No loops.
